Analytical Model
Information for input into a socio-economic analytical model was gathered from interviews with Crow Indian leaders, from U.S. Census reports, and other state and federal informational sources. The model was run on a computer, using 20 different combinations of Scenarios, Alternative Futures, and Labor Force Participation Rates. The results of the most probable of these combinations will be reported in detail here. The structure of the model is outlined in more detail in Appendix I.
To assure Crow tribal input into the preparation of this statement, the Tribe has named two members to serve with the task force in preparing the statement. They have made special contributions to the discussion of socio-economic impacts presented in this section.
Socio-Economic Assumptions
The demographic assumptions utilized to determine the impacts of expanded levels of Westmoreland activity are based on the rates of population growth of the impact area population and on the labor force participation rates of the area's residents.
Fertility rates were derived by taking the average annual number of live births over the period 1969-1971 by age and race of mother for the state of Montana and then calculating rates based on 1970 Census population estimates.
